newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan limits foreigners on warrants holding.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan limits foreigners on warrants holding.

text.p: Taiwan's top securities watchdog body on Friday set a 10-percent ceiling on foreigners holding warrants, the latest instrument to be pioneered in Taiwan's liberalising financial system.
"Each overseas Chinese or foreigner...will only be allowed to hold up to 10 percent of the total number of each warrant issue," the Securities and Exchange Commission said in a statement.
The commission said these investors would also be required to buy warrants in cash.
The commission on Monday announced that 31 listed firms were qualified for warrant issues.

In a long-expected decree effective from June 1, the commission said local and foreign banks or securities brokerages with T$3 billion or more in registered capital could issue warrants on qualified shares.

To qualify, a listed firm's Taiwan shares must have a total market value, based on May 31 closing prices, of more than T$25 billion, with at least 20 percent of their shares circulating in the market between January 31 and April 30.
Listed firms must have more than 15,000 shareholders -- at least 7,000 of whom hold 1,000 to 50,000 shares.
